title: What Is RxJS? Observables and Reactive Thinking

questions.prompt: Which description best fits an RxJS Observable?

options.text: A lazy, push-based collection of multiple values delivered over time
An eager container that resolves exactly one value
A synchronous array that you index into
A function the consumer pulls values from one at a time

questions.explanation: An Observable is lazy (runs on subscribe), push-based (the producer decides when to emit), and can deliver many values over time before completing or erroring.

questions.prompt: In the producer/consumer grid, which cell does an Observable occupy?

options.text: Push + multiple values
Push + single value
Pull + multiple values
Pull + single value

questions.explanation: Observable = push + multiple. A Promise is push + single, a Function is pull + single, and an Iterator is pull + multiple.

questions.prompt: Which statements about how an Observable differs from a Promise are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: An Observable is lazy — the producer only runs when you subscribe
An Observable can emit many values, not just one
An Observable can be cancelled with unsubscribe()
An Observable must always emit asynchronously

questions.explanation: Observables are lazy, multi-value, and cancellable. They can emit synchronously OR asynchronously — it is the Promise that is always async (and eager and single-value).

options.text: A Subscription object you can later unsubscribe()
The first value the Observable emits
A Promise that resolves with all the values
The Observable itself, for chaining

questions.explanation: subscribe() returns a Subscription representing the running execution. You read emitted values inside the next callback, and cancel via subscription.unsubscribe().

questions.prompt: An Observable does no work until something calls this method. Type the method name (no parentheses).
questions.explanation: Observables are lazy: the producer function runs only when subscribe() is called, and each subscribe() starts a fresh execution.

questions.prompt: By convention, a variable holding an Observable is often named with which suffix?

options.text: A trailing $, e.g. results$
A trailing _obs, e.g. results_obs
A leading rx, e.g. rxResults
An trailing !, e.g. results!

questions.explanation: The community convention is a trailing '$' (sometimes called Finnish notation) to signal that a value is a stream/Observable.
